system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Review of Seller’s Updated SPA & Disclosure Letter – Project Kestrel  
**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team  
**Reference:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook (baseline: 25%/AUD 6M cap, 24-month claim period, specific disclosure, independent title proof, etc.)  
**Status of Seller draft:** Marked “FINAL” by Seller; **not** accepted by Buyer. The “Reviewer Efficiency Note” is a tactical framing device – it has no contractual force and does not reflect Buyer agreement.

---

### 1. MATERIAL DEPARTURES FROM PLAYBOOK (ranked by risk)

| # | Issue | Seller Position | Playbook Requirement | Gap / Risk |
|---|-------|-----------------|----------------------|------------|
| **1** | **General Warranty Cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8M (Cl. 12.1) | **25% / AUD 6M** starting position; 20% only with **written Amelia Frost authority** (none given) | Seller has unilaterally imposed Buyer’s *fallback* as “standard”. No principal sign-off exists. |
| **2** | **De Minimis / Basket** | De minimis AUD 25K; basket AUD 250K, **excess-only recovery** (Cl. 12.2) | De minimis **AUD 5K**; basket **AUD 50K**, **first-dollar liability** once basket exceeded | Seller’s thresholds are 5× wider; excess-only recovery shifts material risk to Buyer. |
| **3** | **General Claim Period** | 18 months (Cl. 12.3/13) | **24 months**; 18 months only with **written Amelia Frost approval** (none given) | Seller treats fallback as agreed. |
| **4** | **Fundamental / Title Warranties** | “Subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity” | **Separate regime**: 100% cap, **≥6 years**, **outside** general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Seller collapses fundamental protections into the weakened general regime – **unacceptable**. |
| **5** | **Fraud / Wilful Misconduct Carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy & non-reliance apply to **“all Claims of any nature”** (Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) | **Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance** – to maximum enforceable extent; **no waiver permitted** | Seller’s clause would bar fraud claims – **legally dangerous and commercially untenable**. |
| **6** | **Disclosure Standard** | **General disclosure** of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012) + public registers + statutory registers (Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) | **Specific fair disclosure only**; **reject** whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure | Seller’s “catch-all” disclosure defeats warranty protection; Buyer cannot rely on warranties for anything in the data room. |
| **7** | **Buyer Knowledge Exclusion** | **Blanket bar**: no claim for any matter known to Buyer *or its advisers*, including matters “discoverable” from data room/public records (Cl. 8.3) | **Delete blanket exclusion**; any knowledge qualifier requires **named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**; **never** excuses title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnity | Seller shifts due-diligence risk entirely to Buyer; “discoverable” standard is objectively impossible to police. |
| **8** | **Bluefen Consent (Material Customer)** | **Reasonable endeavours**; consent deemed satisfied **on delivery of counterparty’s written consent** (Cl. 3/6.3) | **Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion**; **not** consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours **insufficient** for material consent | No certainty consent will arrive or that conditions (Cl. 11.3) are met; Buyer bears revenue risk (~30% FY26). |
| **9** | **Riverlark Debt / Security Release** | Release **following Completion** (Cl. 2/7) – no payout at Completion | **Current payout from Completion funds**, **effective security releases**; post-Completion release only with **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** | ~AUD 3.2M debt remains outstanding at Completion; security stays on Target’s assets; Seller has no binding commitment to repay. |
| **10** | **Employee Completion Bonuses (DD-005)** | AUD 420K **“matter for the Seller”**; **not itemised in funds flow** | **Specific line item or Seller-funded**; on-costs (payroll tax, super) **must be included**; funds flow must **not silently exclude** | Buyer may inherit AUD 420K+ liability post-Completion with no price adjustment. |
| **11** | **Ironquay IP Indemnity (DD-004/010)** | Narrow indemnity limited to **SOW3 payment only** (Cl. 11.1); AUD 180K open, **no independent verification** | **Broaden indemnity**, preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180K **not independently verified either way** | Seller treats unverified amount as settled; Buyer exposed to IP ownership/liability gaps. |
| **12** | **Tax / IP Warranties** | “Settled under the general regime above” | **Remain OPEN**; assume **no unlimited liability** and **no resolution** | Seller attempts to fold open items into the already-weak general regime. |
| **13** | **Title Evidence** | Share register at DD-012 **only** | **Independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is **internal**, not independent | No external verification (ASIC search, legal opinion, etc.); Seller refuses to provide standard comfort. |
| **14** | **Sandbar Supplier Renewals (AUD 330K)** | “Ordinary-course operating costs” – no further detail | **Assess**; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction – but **must be evaluated** for accrual/termination risk | Disclosure Letter §8 confirms no clarity on unavoidability/termination; requires diligence, not assumption. |
| **15** | **Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006)** | “Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material” (Cl. 4.6/Sch. 6) | **Preserve logs, investigate, require updates**; **assume NO confirmed breach** – but **must contractually protect** against future notification duty/loss | Seller’s language risks waiving Buyer’s right to claim if breach later confirmed; needs specific indemnity/undertaking. |

---

### 2. KEY REASONING ON SELECTED HIGH-IMPACT ITEMS

#### **A. Limitation Package (Cap / Thresholds / Time / Fundamental Regime / Fraud Carve-out)**
The Seller has packaged the *entire* limitation structure (Cl. 12.1–12.3, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, Fundamental/Title treatment) as “STANDARD” and “agreed”. **None of it is agreed.**  
- The 20% cap is Buyer’s *conditional* fallback – **no principal sign-off**.  
- Thresholds are 5× playbook; excess-only recovery is a **major risk transfer**.  
- 18-month period is a *fallback* – **no approval**.  
- Collapsing Fundamental/Title into general regime **eliminates the separate 100%/6-year protection** the playbook mandates.  
- Applying limitations to “all Claims of any nature” **excludes fraud** – legally precarious and commercially unacceptable.  
**→ Every element must be redlined to playbook baselines.**

#### **B. Disclosure & Buyer Knowledge – The “Double Shield”**
Seller’s general disclosure (whole data room + public registers) **combined** with the blanket buyer-knowledge bar (including “discoverable” matters) means:  
- Buyer **cannot claim** for anything in the data room (general disclosure).  
- Buyer **cannot claim** for anything its advisers *could have found* (knowledge bar).  
This **eviscinates** warranty protection. Playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and **named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry** only. The “discoverable” standard is **objectively unworkable** and must be deleted.

#### **C. Bluefen Consent – Revenue Concentration Risk**
~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD ~3.6M) sits behind a change-control consent (DD-002, Cl. 11.2–11.3). Seller offers only **reasonable endeavours** and **consent-on-delivery**.  
- No evidence consent has been sought, let alone obtained.  
- No evidence conditions (Cl. 11.3) are satisfied.  
- If consent fails post-Completion, Buyer bears the revenue loss with **no recourse** (warranties neutered by disclosure/knowledge bars).  
**→ Condition Precedent: effective consent + condition satisfaction evidence before Completion.**

#### **D. Riverlark – Debt-Free/Cash-Free Mechanics Broken**
AUD ~3.2M facility remains outstanding; security undischarged. Seller proposes **post-Completion
